$comment: Best-effort revenue estimates from PA budget office, IFO analyses, and prior gubernatorial proposals. All numbers are mid-range; treat as informative, not precise. Real revenue depends on tax rate, implementation, ramp-up, and economic conditions. Sources cited per row. Deficit updated to IFO's post-enactment FY 2026-27 General Fund Budget Update (July 2026), via Commonwealth Foundation.

proposals.name: Tax recreational cannabis
proposals.description: Pennsylvania is one of the few states without legal recreational cannabis. Gov. Shapiro's FY 2026-27 budget estimates $729M in year-one revenue from taxes and one-time licensing fees; the IFO puts mature recurring yield lower as license fees drop off.
proposals.statusDetail: Proposed in Gov. Shapiro's FY 2026-27 budget; blocked in PA Senate
proposals.sourceDetail: Shapiro FY 2026-27 executive budget; PA IFO analyses

proposals.name: Tax skill games
proposals.description: The slot-like "skill game" terminals in PA bars and convenience stores operate in a legal gray area with no state tax. Shapiro proposed a 52% tax rate in FY 2026-27, projecting ~$766M in year-one revenue; industry estimates are lower.
proposals.statusDetail: Active in current session; rate and regulatory structure still contested
proposals.sourceDetail: Gov. Shapiro FY 2026-27 budget; legislative fiscal notes

proposals.name: Severance tax on natural gas
proposals.description: Pennsylvania is the only major natural gas–producing state without a traditional severance tax. We collect an "impact fee" instead, which brings in roughly a quarter of what a 5% severance tax would. The creative version: pair it with a faster corporate tax cut so it's a deal, not just a grab.
proposals.statusDetail: Proposed repeatedly since the Marcellus boom; blocked by industry lobby
proposals.sourceDetail: Prior Wolf-era budget proposals; PA Dept of Revenue analyses

proposals.name: Broaden sales tax to services & digital
proposals.description: PA's 6% sales tax applies to goods but exempts most services and the digital economy — subscriptions, streaming, consulting, SaaS. The tax code was designed for a 1970s goods economy. Broadening the base (even while modestly cutting the rate) generates billions in recurring revenue that grows with the modern economy rather than against it.
proposals.statusDetail: No active bill; politically heavy — would require broad legislative coalition
proposals.sourceDetail: PA IFO tax structure analyses; peer-state service-tax models (OH, MD, DC)

proposals.name: End the data center tax exemption
proposals.description: Act 7 of 2017 (expanded by HB 952 in 2022) waives the 6% PA sales tax on data center equipment — a corporate giveaway that has grown significantly as Amazon ($20B Salem Township), Microsoft (Three Mile Island), and others build major facilities here. Repeal or sunset the exemption rather than give away the boom.
proposals.statusDetail: No active repeal bill; would require sunsetting Act 7
proposals.sourceDetail: Act 7 of 2017; HB 952 of 2022; PA Dept of Revenue exemption analyses

proposals.name: Close the "Delaware loophole"
proposals.description: Combined corporate reporting — used by roughly half of US states — prevents multi-state corporations from shifting profits to no-tax-state subsidiaries to avoid PA corporate tax.
proposals.statusDetail: Repeatedly proposed; opposed by business lobby
proposals.sourceDetail: PA Dept of Revenue analyses; multiple gubernatorial budget proposals

proposals.name: Industrial power consumption surcharge
proposals.description: A per-MWh surcharge on industrial-scale power consumers (data centers, crypto mining, large industrial loads). Targets facilities that strain the PJM grid and drive up rates for residential customers — without raising bills for ordinary Pennsylvanians.
proposals.statusDetail: Pre-bill stage; analogous proposals exist in OH and VA
